```plato

    // True when `p` clears every point already accepted in the earlier half of its
    // 5x5 cell block: the two rows above in full, and the cells left of column `i`
    // in the row being built. `above1` is full width, so it also fixes the column
    // count; `row` holds only the columns decided so far.
    PoissonIsFree(p: Point2D, region: Bounds2D, radius: Number, above2: Array<Point2D>,
        above1: Array<Point2D>, row: Array<Point2D>, i: Integer): Boolean
    {
        var free = true;
        var d = -2;
        while (d <= 2)
        {
            var c = i + d;
            if (c >= 0 && c < above1.Count)
            {
                free = free && PoissonSlotFree(p, region, radius, above2, c)
                            && PoissonSlotFree(p, region, radius, above1, c);
                if (d < 0)
                {
                    free = free && PoissonSlotFree(p, region, radius, row, c);
                }
            }
            d = d + 1;
        }
        return free;
    }

    // The accepted point of cell (i, j), or the empty sentinel when `attempts`
    // darts all landed outside the region or inside somebody's radius.
    PoissonCellPoint(region: Bounds2D, radius: Number, attempts: Integer, seed: Integer,
        i: Integer, j: Integer, above2: Array<Point2D>, above1: Array<Point2D>,
        row: Array<Point2D>): Point2D
    {
        var accepted = EmptyCellPoint(region, radius);
        var a = 0;
        while (a < attempts)
        {
            if (IsEmptyCell(accepted, region, radius))
            {
                var candidate = PoissonCandidate(region, radius, seed, i, j, a);
                if (region.Contains(candidate))
                {
                    if (PoissonIsFree(candidate, region, radius, above2, above1, row, i))
                    {
                        accepted = candidate;
                    }
                }
            }
            a = a + 1;
        }
        return accepted;
    }

    // One full-width row of the background grid, left to right, empty cells
    // included. The row is kept whole because the two rows below it index into it
    // by column.
    PoissonRow(region: Bounds2D, radius: Number, attempts: Integer, seed: Integer,
        j: Integer, above2: Array<Point2D>, above1: Array<Point2D>): Array<Point2D>
    {
        var row = Point2D.NoPoints;
        var i = 0;
        while (i < above1.Count)
        {
            row = row.Append(PoissonCellPoint(region, radius, attempts, seed, i, j,
                above2, above1, row));
            i = i + 1;
        }
        return row;
    }

    // The occupied cells of one row, in column order. Rows are compacted as they
    // are finished rather than the whole grid at the end, which keeps every
    // intermediate array short.
    PoissonRowPoints(region: Bounds2D, radius: Number, row: Array<Point2D>): Array<Point2D>
    {
        var kept = Point2D.NoPoints;
        var c = 0;
        while (c < row.Count)
        {
            if (IsEmptyCell(row[c], region, radius).Not)
            {
                kept = kept.Append(row[c]);
            }
            c = c + 1;
        }
        return kept;
    }

    // Poisson-disk points over the region: no two closer than `radius`, in
    // row-major cell order. A non-positive radius yields no points.
    // Precondition: `attempts` is positive — thirty is the usual choice and the
    // one `PoissonDiskPattern2D` documents.
    PoissonDiskPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, radius: Number, attempts: Integer,
        seed: Integer): Array<Point2D>
    {
        var columns = PoissonColumns(region, radius);
        var rows = PoissonRows(region, radius);
        var blank = columns.MapRange(c => EmptyCellPoint(region, radius));
        var above2 = blank;
        var above1 = blank;
        var points = Point2D.NoPoints;
        var j = 0;
        while (j < rows)
        {
            var row = PoissonRow(region, radius, attempts, seed, j, above2, above1);
            points = points.Concatenate(PoissonRowPoints(region, radius, row));
            above2 = above1;
            above1 = row;
            j = j + 1;
        }
        return points;
    }

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: PoissonDiskPattern2D): Array<Point2D>
        => PoissonDiskPoints2D(self.Region, self.MinimumDistance, self.MaxAttempts, self.Seed);

    //==
    // # Blue noise
    //
    // `BlueNoisePattern2D` asks for a COUNT, and Poisson-disk sampling takes a
    // RADIUS and reports whatever count saturates. The two are joined by the
    // saturation density: random sequential adsorption of disks jams at a coverage
    // of about 0.547, which puts about 0.7 * area / radius^2 points on the plane.
    // Generation therefore picks the radius that saturates at somewhat more than
    // the count asked for and thins the result back down.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_sequential_adsorption

    // The Poisson-disk radius whose saturated set holds about a fifth more than
    // `count` points over the region. The surplus is what the thinning below
    // spends, and it also absorbs the shortfall of a sweep that gives each cell
    // only a bounded number of darts.
    BlueNoiseRadius(region: Bounds2D, count: Integer): Number
        => count <= 0 ? 0.0 : (0.7 * RegionArea(region) / (count.ToNumber * 1.2)).Sqrt;

    // The points thinned evenly down to `count`: point i survives when it is the
    // last one mapping to its slot of the target count, which drops a uniform
    // fraction spread through the whole scan instead of a block of it. Exactly
    // `count` points come back when there are at least that many; a shorter input
    // comes back unchanged. Thinning cannot make a set less blue in the way a
    // prefix would — every surviving pair is still at least a radius apart — but
    // it does leave the set no longer maximal, which the low-frequency end of the
    // spectrum registers.
    ThinnedPoints2D(count: Integer, points: Array<Point2D>): Array<Point2D>
    {
        var kept = Point2D.NoPoints;
        var i = 0;
        while (i < points.Count)
        {
            if (points.Count <= count || (i * count) / points.Count != ((i + 1) * count) / points.Count)
            {
                kept = kept.Append(points[i]);
            }
            i = i + 1;
        }
        return kept;
    }
```
